product: Claude's Microsoft 365 connector (Outlook, SharePoint, OneDrive, Teams)
description: "An Anthropic-hosted integration that enables Claude to securely access Microsoft 365 services (Outlook, SharePoint, OneDrive, Teams) through user-delegated permissions." A Global Administrator consents once for the tenant; each user then reaches only what they already have permission for, over OAuth 2.0 On-Behalf-Of. The rows are the connector's tool tables read as capabilities. Lab 01 read this page on 12 September as read-only; on 15 September it lists write tools too, and both readings are recorded.

reach_names.host: SharePoint sites and OneDrive files the user can already open — searched tenant-wide
reach_names.tenant: the Microsoft Entra tenant the administrator consented for; the user's mailbox, shared mailboxes they are delegated to, and Teams chats
reach_names.world: anyone reachable by mail from the user's address

blocked.blocked_by: Microsoft's tenancy rule for the connector — a work or school account is required

blocked.what: other users' private files or emails
blocked.blocked_by: the delegated permission model — the connector reaches what the signed-in user already reaches, and no more
blocked.why: "Users can't access other users' private files or emails"; delegated permissions reach only what the user already can

blocked.blocked_by: Microsoft's search — the archive is a separate store the connector's search does not cover
blocked.why: "Email search doesn't reach a user's separate Online Archive (In-Place Archive) mailbox"

blocked.blocked_by: the connector's design — the underlying search is tenant-wide, so *.Selected permissions are not supported
blocked.why: "Site-specific permissioning (using *.Selected permissions) is not supported because the underlying search is tenant-wide"

blocked.blocked_by: the connector's tool surface — the write tools are mail and Teams, and no file-write tool is listed
blocked.why: no write tool for files is listed; the write tools are mail and Teams

grant.control: delegated Entra permissions Mail.Read, Mail.Read.Shared and Chat.Read — consented once by a Global Administrator, revocable per permission in Entra
grant.note: the user's mailbox, "shared mailboxes they've been granted delegate access to … including full access and folder-level delegation", and Teams chats. Shared-mailbox access is stated as read-only via Mail.Read.Shared.

grant.control: Mail.Send, delegated; "Revoke … in Entra" is the off switch, and it is the administrator's, not the user's
grant.note: outlook_send_mail — "Send an email as the user." To any address. Listed under Write tools on the same page whose read section says the connector "provides read-only access to" its sources.

grant.control: delegated Sites.Read.All and Files.Read / Files.Read.All; "Users cannot bypass SharePoint sharing settings or folder permissions"
grant.note: "SharePoint search requires Sites.Read.All permission. Site-specific permissioning (using *.Selected permissions) is not supported because the underlying search is tenant-wide." Everything the user can already open, across the tenant.

grant.control: delegated permissions; "Multi-tenant isolation is cryptographically enforced through digitally signed access tokens"
grant.note: "Users can only access Microsoft 365 data they already have permission for." Anthropic hosts the connector and holds the token.

a work mailbox carries password resets, MFA codes and shared credentials sent between colleagues; a SharePoint estate carries key files and configuration. Reading either reads those. Inferred, not documented.

contradictions.advertised: "The connector provides read-only access to:" (the heading over the read tools)
contradictions.permitted: a "Write tools" table on the same page: outlook_send_mail (Mail.Send), outlook_trash_thread and outlook_batch_delete_messages (Mail.ReadWrite)

contradictions.advertised: "Shared mailbox access remains read-only, via the Mail.Read.Shared permission"
contradictions.permitted: outlook_send_mail "Send an email as the user" — whether it can send from a shared mailbox is not stated

contradictions.advertised: Lab 01, 12 September: the page read as a read-only connector
contradictions.permitted: 15 September: the same page lists ten write tools. The page moved between the two readings; which capabilities a tenant consented to before the change is not stated

not_in_grammar.what: trash, untrash and batch-delete mail; create and update drafts
not_in_grammar.why: the 23 primitives have delete.file.host and write.file.host; a message is not a file, and no primitive names deleting or drafting one

not_in_grammar.what: search the calendar and find meeting availability
not_in_grammar.why: no primitive reads a calendar; create.schedule.* creates jobs, not events

not_in_grammar.what: send Teams messages and create chats
not_in_grammar.why: send.message.world covers it loosely; a Teams post reaches the tenant, and whether it reaches federated external chats is open

research_needed.question: Are the write tools on for every plan by default, or gated behind a separate administrator consent of Mail.Send?
research_needed.how: Anthropic's connector page and the Entra consent record for the application, quoted. Do not send.

research_needed.question: Does Teams sending reach federated (external) chats, or only the tenant?
research_needed.how: Anthropic's page for ChatMessage.Send scope and Microsoft Graph's description of that permission.

research_needed.question: "Delegated permissions inherently respect Microsoft 365 data loss prevention (DLP) policies" — enforced by Graph on read, or by the connector after read?
research_needed.how: Microsoft Graph documentation on DLP and delegated access; at best self-reported on Anthropic's side.

research_needed.question: Do connector reads appear in Purview audit logs, and under whose identity?
research_needed.how: Microsoft Purview audit documentation for Graph delegated access.
